title: Level 10: UART Serial Transmit — Streaming Data to a PC
aim: To configure the ATmega328P's USART peripheral to transmit ASCII text and numeric data over a serial connection at 9600 baud to a PC terminal, without using the Arduino Serial library.
objective: Understand UART framing (start bit, data bits, stop bit), baud rate calculation using UBRR registers, USART control registers (UCSRB, UCSRC), and polling-based byte transmission via UDR0.
theory:
UART — Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter

UART is the simplest serial communication protocol — two wires (TX and RX), no shared clock. Data is transmitted one bit at a time at a pre-agreed rate called the baud rate (bits per second). The ATmega328P's USART0 peripheral implements UART in hardware and maps to PD0 (RX) and PD1 (TX) — Arduino Uno pins 0 and 1.

UART Frame Format

Each byte is transmitted as a frame:

  • Start bit — 1 bit low (line goes from idle-HIGH to LOW)
  • Data bits — 5–8 bits, LSB first
  • Parity bit — optional error detection (None, Even, Odd)
  • Stop bit — 1 or 2 bits high

The most common format is 8N1: 8 data bits, No parity, 1 stop bit. This is 10 bits total per byte.

Baud Rate Calculation

The USART baud rate is derived from the system clock using the UBRR (USART Baud Rate Register) divider. In normal speed mode (U2X=0):

UBRR = (F_CPU / (16 × baud)) − 1

For 9600 baud at 16 MHz: UBRR = (16,000,000 / (16 × 9600)) − 1 = 104.17 → 103 (rounds down). This gives a true baud rate of 9615 bps — only 0.16% error, well within the 3% UART tolerance.

USART Control Registers

  • UBRR0H:UBRR0L — Baud rate divider (high and low bytes). Write the UBRR value here.
  • UCSR0A — Status register. Bit UDRE0 = 1 when UDR0 (transmit buffer) is empty and ready for the next byte.
  • UCSR0B — Control register B. TXEN0 (bit 3) enables the transmitter; RXEN0 (bit 4) enables the receiver. Setting TXEN0 hands pin PD1 (TX) to the USART hardware.
  • UCSR0C — Frame format register. UCSZ01:UCSZ00 = 1:1 selects 8 data bits. UPM01:UPM00 = 0:0 = No parity. USBS0 = 0 = 1 stop bit. Together: 8N1.

Transmitting a Byte (Polling)

Before writing the next byte to UDR0 (USART Data Register 0), you must wait for the transmit buffer to be empty by polling the UDRE0 bit in UCSR0A. When UDRE0 = 1, the previous byte has been loaded into the shift register and UDR0 is ready: while(!(UCSR0A & (1<<UDRE0))); UDR0 = byte;

USB-to-Serial Conversion

Modern computers don't have RS-232 serial ports. The Arduino Uno includes a second microcontroller (ATmega16U2) configured as a USB-to-Serial bridge. When the MCU transmits on TX (PD1), the bridge converts it to USB CDC and appears as a COM/ttyUSB port on the PC. Connect with a serial terminal at matching baud rate.

pretest.question: What does UART stand for?
pretest.explanation: UART = Universal Asynchronous Receiver-Transmitter. 'Asynchronous' means no shared clock signal between sender and receiver — baud rate must be pre-agreed.

pretest.question: What is 8N1 UART format?
options: 8 data bits, No parity, 1 stop bit
8 start bits, N data bits, 1 stop bit
pretest.explanation: 8N1 is the most common UART format: 8 data bits, No parity checking, 1 stop bit. Total frame = 10 bits (1 start + 8 data + 1 stop).

pretest.question: Using UBRR = (F_CPU / (16 × baud)) − 1, what UBRR value gives 9600 baud at 16 MHz?
pretest.explanation: UBRR = (16,000,000 / (16 × 9600)) − 1 = 104.17 − 1 ≈ 103. The 0.16% error is within UART's 3% tolerance.

pretest.question: Which bit in UCSR0B enables the UART transmitter?
pretest.explanation: TXEN0 (Transmitter Enable 0, bit 3 of UCSR0B) enables the USART transmitter. When set, pin PD1 (TX) is controlled by the USART hardware.

pretest.question: Which register is written to transmit a byte over UART?
pretest.explanation: UDR0 (USART Data Register 0) is the transmit/receive data register. Writing a byte to UDR0 places it in the transmit buffer — hardware shifts it out bit-by-bit.

pretest.question: What must be checked before writing to UDR0?
pretest.explanation: UDRE0 (USART Data Register Empty, bit 5 of UCSR0A) must be 1 before writing to UDR0. If UDR0 is written while UDRE0=0, the byte being shifted out may be corrupted.

pretest.question: Which ATmega328P pin is the UART TX (transmit) output?
pretest.explanation: USART0 TX is on PD1 (Arduino Uno Digital Pin 1). PD0 is USART0 RX. Note: connected to the USB-Serial bridge on the Arduino board.

pretest.question: How many total bits are in one 8N1 UART frame?
pretest.explanation: 8N1 frame: 1 start bit + 8 data bits + 0 parity bits + 1 stop bit = 10 bits total. At 9600 baud, this gives 9600/10 = 960 bytes per second.

pretest.question: What is the purpose of the start bit in UART?
options: Signal the receiver that a new frame is beginning (line transitions from idle HIGH to LOW)
pretest.explanation: The UART line is idle-HIGH. The start bit (logic LOW) is the falling edge that the receiver detects to begin sampling data bits at the agreed baud rate.

pretest.question: For higher speed communication (115200 baud), what UBRR value is needed at 16 MHz?
pretest.explanation: UBRR = (16,000,000 / (16 × 115200)) − 1 = 8.68 − 1 ≈ 8. The actual baud rate is 16M/(16×9) = 111,111 bps — 3.5% error, borderline but usually works.

procedure: Include #include <avr/io.h>. Define #define F_CPU 16000000UL and #define BAUD 9600. Calculate UBRR: #define UBRR_VAL ((F_CPU / (16UL * BAUD)) - 1) = 103.
Set the baud rate by loading UBRR_VAL split into high and low bytes: UBRR0H = (UBRR_VAL >> 8); UBRR0L = UBRR_VAL;. The high byte must be written first.
Configure the frame format in UCSR0C: 8 data bits (UCSZ01=1, UCSZ00=1), 1 stop bit (USBS0=0), no parity (UPM01=0, UPM00=0): UCSR0C = (1 << UCSZ01) | (1 << UCSZ00);.
Enable the USART transmitter in UCSR0B: UCSR0B = (1 << TXEN0);. The TX pin (PD1) is now controlled by hardware USART. Note: no DDRD manipulation needed — TXEN0 overrides DDR.
Write a transmit helper function: void uart_tx(uint8_t byte) { while (!(UCSR0A & (1 << UDRE0))); UDR0 = byte; }. This polls UDRE0 until the buffer is empty, then loads the next byte.
Write a string transmit function: void uart_print(const char *s) { while(*s) uart_tx(*s++); }. This iterates through a null-terminated C string, sending each character ASCII code.

In the main loop, send a test message followed by a newline every second: uart_print("Hello from ATmega328P!\r\n"); _delay_ms(1000);. Also print the ADC value (from Exp 9) to show numeric data transmission.
Open a serial terminal (Arduino Serial Monitor, PuTTY, or screen) at 9600 baud on the correct COM/ttyUSB port. Verify 'Hello from ATmega328P!' appears every second.

posttest.question: At 9600 baud with 8N1 framing (10 bits/byte), what is the maximum byte throughput?
posttest.explanation: Throughput = baud / bits_per_frame = 9600 / 10 = 960 bytes per second.

posttest.question: What happens if the receiver's baud rate doesn't match the transmitter's?
options: Framing errors — received bytes are corrupted because sampling occurs at wrong times
posttest.explanation: Baud mismatch causes the receiver to sample data bits at the wrong moments, leading to framing errors and incorrect byte values.

posttest.question: How does the ATmega328P's USB connection allow UART communication with a PC?
options: A second MCU (ATmega16U2) bridges UART to USB CDC, appearing as a COM port
posttest.explanation: The Arduino Uno has an ATmega16U2 USB-to-Serial converter that bridges the ATmega328P's USART0 to a USB CDC interface visible as a virtual COM port on the PC.

posttest.question: To transmit 'A' (ASCII 65), what byte do you write to UDR0?
options: All of the above are equivalent
posttest.explanation: In C, 'A', 65, and 0x41 are all the same 8-bit value. Writing any of them to UDR0 transmits the ASCII character 'A'.

posttest.question: What does \r\n mean in UART output and why is it used?
options: Carriage Return (CR) + Line Feed (LF) — Windows terminals need both for proper newline
posttest.explanation: \r is CR (ASCII 13, moves cursor to start of line), \n is LF (ASCII 10, moves cursor down one line). Windows terminals require both; Linux terminals usually accept just \n.

posttest.question: What is the UDRE0 flag and when is it set?
options: Set when the transmit data register (UDR0) is empty and ready for the next byte
posttest.explanation: UDRE0 (USART Data Register Empty) in UCSR0A is set HIGH when UDR0 is empty. Polling this ensures you don't overwrite a byte that hasn't been sent yet.

posttest.question: What is a watchdog timer used for?
posttest.explanation: WDT automatically resets the MCU if not periodically cleared.

posttest.question: Which is NOT a valid ATmega328P port?
posttest.explanation: ATmega328P has Port B, C, and D only.

posttest.question: What happens to SRAM when power is removed?
In an ISR, interrupts are automatically:
posttest.explanation: AVR clears the I-bit in SREG on ISR entry.

feedback: Outstanding! UART serial communication is the backbone of embedded debugging and PC interfacing. Every GPS module, Bluetooth chip, GSM modem, and GNSS receiver communicates via UART — you now know exactly how it works at the register level.
